title: Note staleness lifecycle: create baseline → lazy refresh → verifyNote
answers: How does a note become stale?
How is a stale note re-verified?
What triggers refresh of note status?
Where are dependency hashes computed and compared?
body:
Note staleness lifecycle: create baseline → lazy refresh → verify

No file watcher; staleness is detected lazily.

1. Create: src/ops.js:createNote → extractDeps (parses `path:Symbol` from body) → resolveDeps → src/deps.js:hashDep (findSymbol/blockEnd, sha/norm; falls back to file hash + symbolMissing). Saves verified, verifiedCommit=gitHead(repo), status 'fresh' via src/store.js:Store.put (.thinker/notes/<id>.json).

2. Code edit: nothing happens until something calls refresh.

3. Detect: src/ops.js:refresh → src/deps.js:checkNote (re-hash; reasons: file removed / symbol not found / symbol body changed / file changed) → status 'stale' + stale:{since,changed}. Hashes matching again (revert) flips back to fresh; 'invalid' notes are skipped.

4. refresh callers: ops.js:orient (refreshFirst=true by default; pass refreshFirst=false to skip), ops.js:lookup (always calls refresh), cli.js cases list/check/verify, optional git post-commit hook (init --git-hook → cli.js check --quiet).

5. Serve: src/rank.js:rank multiplies stale score by 0.6; renderNote adds '⚠ STALE' line. Invalid scores -1 (never served).

6. Re-verify: src/ops.js:verifyNote (via cli.js verify [ids]/verifyAll or check --verify): for non-behavior notes, prompt from ops.js:gitDiffFor (diff from note.verifiedCommit) + deps.js:symbolText → src/llm.js:complete with VERIFY_SCHEMA, model store.config().verifyModel (default haiku); for notes of kind 'behavior', delegates to verifyBehavior. still_valid: re-hash, fresh, confidence +0.05; update: also replaces body, old body pushed to history; invalid: status invalid + invalidReason.

Symbol body changes detected in src/deps.js:checkNote via hash mismatch.
